references.text: Peter asks the same question about why he cannot follow Jesus now, and Jesus answers that he cannot follow yet but will follow later.
Peter draws a sword to defend Jesus, an action that shows his willingness to give his life, even though Jesus tells him to put away the sword.
Peter again affirms his willingness to die for Jesus, even though he later betrays him, which mirrors his claim in John 13:37.
Peter declares that he is ready to go with Jesus both to prison and to death, but Jesus predicts that he will deny him before a rooster crows.
Peter says that he is willing to die for Jesus even if everyone else abandons him, which highlights his strong but mistaken self-confidence.
